title: ocidex-pg WAL corruption after force-deleted pod during smart shutdown
description: 2026-10-14 00:33:58 CNPG rolled ocidex-pg-1 for the 1d0cfec resources change (smart shutdown, 1800s grace; clients kept it waiting). 00:34:37 admin force-deleted the pod via k9s (apiserver audit). The new pod started PG on the same local-path PGDATA at 00:34:41 while the old postmaster was alive until 00:35:12 ('postmaster.pid contains wrong PID'). Result: PANIC 'could not locate a valid checkpoint record at 192/F702DB38'. ocidex-pg-dump CronJob has never succeeded, so there is no fresh backup. Recovery: hibernate, copy PGDATA to pgdata.corrupt-20261014, pg_resetwal, amcheck, dump.
close_reason: Recovered: hibernated, copied PGDATA to pgdata.corrupt-20261014 (same PVC), pg_resetwal -x 35651584 -m 65536,1 -O 52352 -o 900000. pg_amcheck clean on 480 relations; fresh dump /dumps/20261014T010507Z (11G, TOC verified). Delete the corrupt copy once satisfied.

Without it there was no fresh backup when ocidex-pg's WAL was corrupted on 2026-10-14 (homelab-8tp). Also alert on backup age.

title: synology-csi: thick LUN first-mkfs discard saturates NAS; took ocidex-pg down
description: 2026-10-13: first mkfs.ext4 of a new 60Gi synology-csi LUN (ocidex-pg-dumps) discarded the whole thick LUN at ~4 MB/s for ~2h. NAS saturation caused iSCSI ping timeouts on the ocidex-pg-2 data LUN (sdh); at 06:32:41 UTC session recovery timed out (120s), writes failed, ext4 aborted journal and remounted read-only. ocidex-pg down 06:32-11:45 UTC. Recovered: hibernate -> remount -> PG crash recovery clean; pg_amcheck run. ocidex-pg-dump CronJob suspended (cc1b2ec) until fixed. Fix options: thin LUNs via StorageClass parameter (type: BLUN / thin), mkfs -E nodiscard via fsType options, or raise iSCSI replacement_timeout. Also: one NAS + single DB instance = no redundancy.
notes: Fixed: f416036 adds formatOptions '-E nodiscard' to SC synology-csi-iscsi (SC recreated 2026-10-13). Canary 60Gi PVC: Running in 126s, no FailedMount, no conn/IO errors. CronJob resumed (c2f2f4e). Follow-ups not done: raise iSCSI replacement_timeout (needs custom iscsi-tools config); DB redundancy (2nd instance or WAL archiving).
close_reason: Fixed in f416036: synology-csi SC formatOptions '-E nodiscard'; 60Gi canary mounted in 126s with no iSCSI errors. ocidex-pg has since moved back to local-path (0fe4e94), so no DB depends on the NAS now.

title: Second PAC controller for the tektonic-ci org GitHub App
description:
Parent: tektonic-uru.3 (tektonic repo, epic tektonic-uru: move tektonic to the tektonic-ci GitHub org).

The PAC GitHub App is private and owned by the personal account, so it cannot be installed on the tektonic-ci org, and it must stay private and personal for pfenerty/* repos. PAC v0.51.0 supports one controller per GitHub App (docs/content/docs/operations/multi-controller.md at v0.51.0, tech preview): each controller reads PAC_CONTROLLER_LABEL / PAC_CONTROLLER_SECRET / PAC_CONTROLLER_CONFIGMAP (already present in release.yaml with the defaults), stamps pipelinesascode.tekton.dev/controller-info on every PipelineRun it creates, and the single shared watcher reads that annotation (pkg/reconciler/reconciler.go controllerInfoForPipelineRun) to report with the right App's credentials. Each App only delivers webhooks for repos it is installed on, so the two controllers never both handle one event.

Plan (all under talos-cluster/flux/apps/pipelines-as-code/):
1. second-controller.yaml, generated NOT hand-written: extend update-manifests.sh to fetch hack/second-controller.py at PAC_VERSION and run it with label tektonic-ci, --controller-image pinned to ghcr.io/tektoncd/pipelines-as-code/pipelines-as-code-controller:$PAC_VERSION (the script defaults to :stable, which would reintroduce the version skew the script's header warns about), --namespace pipelines-as-code, no --ingress-domain (ingress is ours, step 3). Output: Deployment + Service + ConfigMap (tektonic-ci-configmap) + Role/RoleBinding letting the shared controller ServiceAccount update that ConfigMap. Strip anything the OpenShift strip step would also strip.
2. tektonic-ci-secret.enc.yaml (SOPS, same as pipelines-as-code-secret.enc.yaml): keys github-application-id, github-private-key, webhook.secret for the new App.
3. tailscale-ingress: a second Ingress (funnel) for the new controller's Service, own hostname (e.g. pac-webhook-tektonic-ci). Check the tailnet ACL grants funnel to the new node the same way it does for pac-webhook.
4. kustomization.yaml: add the three files.
5. tektonic-ci app in Flux (like apps/ocidex-ci + ocidex-ci.kustomization.yaml): namespace tektonic-ci plus the Repository CRs for tektonic-ci/core (and later reporter-github, cache-gcs). Today the tektonic CR is applied by hand and still points at pfenerty/tektonic; source of truth for its content is tektonic's .tektonic/tektonic-repository.k8s.yaml.
6. apps/renovate/cronjob.yaml renovate-tektonic: repositories ["pfenerty/tektonic"] -> ["tektonic-ci/core"] and give Renovate's credentials access to the org.
7. ServiceMonitor (apps/monitoring-extras/servicemonitor-pac.yaml): check whether its selector picks up the second controller's metrics port; extend if not.

Human steps (GitHub UI):
- Create a GitHub App owned by the tektonic-ci org, visibility 'Only on this account'. Copy permissions and event subscriptions from the existing PAC App's settings page. Webhook URL = the new funnel hostname; webhook secret = the one stored in step 2. Generate the private key.
- Install it on tektonic-ci with 'All repositories' so future provider repos are covered without re-installing.
- Delete the leftover repo webhook on tektonic-ci/core pointing at https://tektonic-eventlistener.bear-velociraptor.ts.net (pre-PAC Triggers listener; confirm nothing still serves it first).
acceptance_criteria: A PR on tektonic-ci/core starts a PipelineRun whose controller-info annotation names tektonic-ci; tektonic's commit statuses and PAC's check land on the PR; pfenerty/* repos still run through the default controller; update-manifests.sh regenerates second-controller.yaml at the pinned version.
notes:
2026-09-26: implemented in draft PR #216 (branch homelab-hsb-tektonic-ci-pac). Correction: tektonic's self-CI was never deployed; it wrote to .tektonic/, which PAC never reads. Fixed in tektonic-ci/core#80. Remaining human steps: generate the App private key, commit tektonic-ci-secret.enc.yaml, make sure the renovate PAT reaches the tektonic-ci org, delete the old tektonic-eventlistener webhook, then merge #80 and #216.
2026-09-26: #216 merged. The tektonic-ci controller is serving webhooks, and the first tektonic self-CI run passed.
close_reason: Done: homelab #216 and #217 merged. The second controller serves tektonic-ci; CI and Renovate are verified.

title: Fix talosctl endpoint resolution across Makefile targets
description: Generated talosconfig has 'endpoints: []' (talosctl gen config never populates it), so any target passing --talosconfig without an explicit --endpoints fails with 'error constructing client: failed to determine endpoints' — hit by upgrade-x86-01. health and kubeconfig were worse: no --talosconfig at all, so they used ~/.talos/config (stale ocidex-dev context). Fix: populate endpoints in the generated talosconfig during generate, add --talosconfig/--endpoints to health/kubeconfig/upgrade-x86-01, and make Makefile a prerequisite of config generation so TALOS_VERSION bumps force a regenerate.
close_reason: Endpoints baked into generated talosconfig; health/kubeconfig/upgrade-x86-01 fixed; Makefile added as generate prerequisite. Verified: talosctl resolves endpoints from repo talosconfig, make health passes.

title: Pin talosctl gen config to TALOS_VERSION and fix upgrade-% talosconfig
description: talosctl client upgraded to v1.14.0. Two breakages: (1) 'talosctl gen config' without --talos-version defaults to the client version and emits v1.14-only documents (DiscoveryServiceConfig, DiscoveryIdentityConfig, UnattendedInstallConfig), which v1.13.9 nodes reject with 'DiscoveryServiceConfig v1alpha1: not registered'. (2) upgrade-% does not pass --talosconfig/--endpoints, so it falls back to ~/.talos/config (context ocidex-dev, endpoint 127.0.0.1:63567) and fails with connection refused.
close_reason: Pinned --talos-version and fixed upgrade-% talosconfig; verified with make validate + make repatch-rpi-01 (applied without reboot)

title: Move etcd off SD cards on RPi4 control-plane nodes
description:
All three control-plane nodes run etcd on a 32GB SD card (mmcblk0, mmc transport, no SSD attached). etcd logs 'slow fdatasync took 1.317s (expected 1s)' and 'leader failed to send out heartbeat on time; leader is overloaded likely from slow disk'. Read-only ranges hit 4-6s.

This is the root cause behind homelab-8md. The work done there (pruner fix, etcd defrag 204MB->46MB, apiserver GOMEMLIMIT, widened leader-election deadlines) is load reduction that makes the SD cards survivable - it does NOT change fdatasync latency. Post-fix etcd still logs 1.3-3.3s applies under CI load.

Options:
1. Attach USB3 SSDs to each RPi4, point install.disk at the USB device in the Talos config, reinstall one node at a time preserving quorum.
2. Zero-hardware alternative: x86-01 already has a 240GB SATA SSD (SanDisk SDSSDXPS) and 16GB RAM at 37% use. Reprovision it as the control-plane node and demote the RPi4s to workers. Costs 3-node HA, but the current 'HA' is three nodes that fail together.
acceptance_criteria: etcd logs show no 'slow fdatasync' warnings under normal CI load; apply request durations stay under 500ms
notes:
Runbook written: talos-cluster/docs/etcd-storage-migration.md

Two options documented, Option A recommended:
A) Keep SD for boot, move EPHEMERAL (currently /dev/mmcblk0p6, 30GB, holds /var/lib/etcd) to a USB SSD via a Talos VolumeConfig document with diskSelector 'match: !system_disk && disk.transport == usb'. Supported config, no reinstall, no EEPROM change. Requires wiping EPHEMERAL once per node (talosctl reset --graceful --system-labels-to-wipe EPHEMERAL --reboot) because VolumeConfig is only honoured at provisioning time - see siderolabs/talos#9394.
B) Full USB boot (literal SD replacement): EEPROM BOOT_ORDER=0xf14, reflash schematic ee21ef4a (rpi_generic, no extensions) to SSD. Off the documented path - Talos RPi docs cover SD only.

Hardware: 3x TLC+DRAM SATA SSD (870 EVO / MX500 - NOT DRAM-less like A400, sync-write latency is the whole point), 3x USB3-SATA adapter with ASM1153E/ASM235CM (avoid JMS567/578 revisions - bad UAS firmware corrupts writes), 3x official RPi 15W PSU.

PREREQUISITE FOUND: machine.install.disk is currently the gen-config default /dev/sda, which does not exist on the RPi4s - but WILL become the USB SSD once attached. Pin it to /dev/mmcblk0 in the controlplane patch before attaching anything.

title: Control-plane instability: kube-controller-manager/scheduler losing leader leases (~1000 restarts each)
description:
Every leader-electing workload in the cluster is crash-looping on 5s Lease GET timeouts.

Evidence (2026-08-01):
- kube-controller-manager-talos-{1q6,byt,fd9}: 1080 / 1059 / 1112 restarts
- kube-scheduler-talos-*: 1064 / 1070 / 1087 restarts
- cilium-operator-*: 202 / 209 restarts
- kube-apiserver-talos-*: 11 / 16 / 5 restarts
- ocidex-operator-dev: 33 restarts in 3h54m

kube-controller-manager fails against 127.0.0.1:7445 (node-local Talos apiserver LB) on the control-plane node itself, so this is not pod-network latency — the apiserver/etcd control plane itself exceeds 5s on a trivial Lease GET.

Measured from an in-cluster pod, 40 sequential GETs of a Lease: median 44ms, but outliers at 2.37s, 2.98s, 5.15s, 5.63s (~10% over 2s, 5% over 5s).

Suspected cause: memory pressure on the three arm64 RPi control-plane nodes, sitting at 93% / 96% / 104% memory (talos-1q6-aue, talos-byt-k6n, talos-fd9-twg). Node MemoryPressure condition is still False, so the kubelet is not evicting — but etcd/apiserver latency is consistent with contention.

Downstream victim: ocidex-vh6 (ocidex-operator crash loop), mitigated there by widening the operator's lease timings — that masks the symptom, it does not fix this.
notes:
VERIFICATION 2026-08-01 02:55 (~10 min after rollout, under active CI load):

IN SCOPE - fixed:
- kube-controller-manager / kube-scheduler / kube-apiserver: 0 restarts across all 3 nodes (were ~1100/~1080/~12). Watch running for 1h.
- etcd quorum held through the 3-node rollout; raft term unchanged at 29986 (no election).
- FailedCreate events 1560 -> 0.
- cilium-operator 2/2 available, 0 restarts.

NOT fixed (expected - root cause is homelab-bwl):
- Lease GET probe, 40 samples via kubectl: median 113ms, p90 196ms, max 3494ms, 2/40 (5%) over 2s.
  Issue baseline was median 44ms in-cluster, ~10% over 2s, 5% over 5s, max 5.63s.
  So: nothing over 5s any more, but multi-second outliers persist at ~5%. That is the SD card.
  My plan target of 'no sample over 2s' was NOT met.
- etcd still logs 'apply request took too long' at 1.3-3.3s under CI load.
- These no longer cost KCM/scheduler leadership only because the renew deadline is now 45s, not 5s.

SEPARATE PROBLEM SPOTTED: ocidex-operator-dev is still crash-looping (14 restarts), losing its lease at
02:49:28 with 'timeout=5s'. The homelab-8md description says ocidex-vh6 already mitigated this by widening
the operator's lease timings - the running pod is still on 5s, so that mitigation is either not deployed or
did not take. Worth re-checking in the ocidex repo. It will keep tripping on the ~5% multi-second outliers
until homelab-bwl is done.
close_reason: Mitigated: pruner fix, etcd defrag, apiserver GOMEMLIMIT and 45s leader-election renew deadlines (talos patches/controlplane.yaml). kube-controller-manager and kube-scheduler show 0 restarts over 2+ days (checked 2026-10-13). The root cause, etcd on SD cards, stays open as homelab-bwl.

title: Make Talos upgrade targets self-unwinding
description: Manual three-step worker upgrade (cnpg-maintenance-on / upgrade / off) is easy to half-complete: a failure between steps leaves Flux suspended and the node cordoned. Fold the maintenance window into upgrade-x86-01 with unwind on failure/interrupt, uncordon on exit in all upgrade targets, retry the CNPG patch when its webhook is briefly unreachable, verify the PDB actually dropped before draining, guard upgrade-104 against the wrong schematic, and run health at the end of upgrade-all.
close_reason: upgrade-x86-01 self-contained with unwind on failure/interrupt; uncordon-on-exit everywhere; webhook retry + PDB precondition; 104 guard; upgrade-all runs health. Maintenance cycle verified live.

title: Only one schedulable worker: control-plane NoSchedule taints leave everything on x86-01
description: All three control-plane nodes carry node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane:NoSchedule despite the README describing allowSchedulingOnControlPlanes: true, so cnpg-system's operator (and most other workloads) can only schedule on talos-jlf-6ro. During a worker drain the operator gets evicted along with everything else and goes Pending, which is what let the PDB come back and deadlock the first upgrade attempt. Options: give the operator a control-plane toleration, or make the control planes schedulable as documented.
notes: 2026-10-13 backlog review: absorbed homelab-k52 (Tekton CI capacity has the same root cause; all CI pods land on x86-01 with no resource quota per pipeline run). Taints still present on all 3 RPi nodes. Fix options: tolerate control-plane taints for arm64-safe workloads, set allowSchedulingOnControlPlanes, or add a second amd64 worker; separately bound CI with a ResourceQuota/LimitRange.

title: Worker Talos upgrades blocked by single-instance CNPG PDB
description: talosctl upgrade drains before reboot; ocidex-pg is a 1-instance CloudNativePG cluster on local-path storage on talos-jlf-6ro (the only amd64 node), so its PDB (minAvailable=1, 0 allowed disruptions) can never permit eviction and the drain times out. Added cnpg-maintenance-on/off targets (nodeMaintenanceWindow with reusePVC) and a DRAIN=false escape hatch, documented in README. title: Tekton Chains: PipelineRun annotation storage exceeds 256KiB, causing sign retry storm
description:
Origin: ocidex-tb9 (filed in the ocidex beads DB).

Every ocidex push PipelineRun ends with chains.tekton.dev/signed=failed after retries=3.
apko-cicd PipelineRuns are signed=true, so the failure is payload-size dependent.

ROOT CAUSE
chains-config sets artifacts.pipelinerun.storage: "tekton, oci"
(talos-cluster/flux/apps/tekton-chains/kustomization.yaml:22). The 'tekton' backend writes
the signed DSSE payload back onto the object as a k8s annotation. With
enable-deep-inspection: true and ocidex's 10 image subjects, the aggregate slsa/v2alpha4
payload exceeds the 262144-byte annotation limit:

  PipelineRun.tekton.dev "ocidex-ocidex-push-lzrqc" is invalid:
  metadata.annotations: Too long: may not be more than 262144 bytes
  (chains/signing.go:265, tekton/tekton.go:76)

PROVENANCE IS NOT LOST. For lzrqc the payload was signed, uploaded to Rekor
(logIndex 2372227296), and the OCI backend pushed the aggregate attestation to all 10
images. Only the redundant annotation copy 422s.

THE ACTUAL COST is the retry storm: the reconciler re-runs the whole sign+store cycle each
requeue. One PipelineRun produced 9 Rekor entries (8 redundant, polluting the public
transparency log) and 90 OCI attestation uploads (10 images x 9 attempts), ~2.5 min of
controller time and ghcr push traffic per push run -- plus a signed=failed status that
misrepresents reality.

FIX
Set artifacts.pipelinerun.storage: "oci" (drop 'tekton'). TaskRun storage stays
"tekton, oci" -- those payloads are small and succeed. Update the storage row in
apps/tekton-chains/README.md to match.

TRADEOFF: apko-cicd loses its currently-working PipelineRun annotation copy. Acceptable --
it is redundant with the OCI + Rekor copies, and chains-config is global so the setting
cannot be scoped per namespace.

Nothing consumes the annotation: ocidex internal/enrichment/provenance/parse.go:91 reads
chains.tekton.dev/transparency from the OCI manifest annotations, not the k8s object.
acceptance_criteria:
- chains-config live value artifacts.pipelinerun.storage == 'oci'
- Next ocidex push PipelineRun carries chains.tekton.dev/signed=true with no retries annotation
- Controller logs show 1 Rekor upload and 10 OCI attestation uploads for that run (not 9 and 90)
- cosign verify-attestation still succeeds against ghcr.io/pfenerty/ocidex-api
notes:
Files: talos-cluster/flux/apps/tekton-chains/kustomization.yaml (artifacts.pipelinerun.storage: "tekton, oci" -> "oci"), talos-cluster/flux/apps/tekton-chains/README.md (split TaskRun/PipelineRun storage rows + new 'Why PipelineRun storage omits tekton' section).

Approach: dropped the 'tekton' (k8s annotation) storage backend for PipelineRuns only. TaskRun storage unchanged. Commit fda1edc, pushed; Flux reconciled and the live cm now reads artifacts.pipelinerun.storage=oci, artifacts.taskrun.storage='tekton, oci'.

Verified BEFORE committing by patching the live cm and force-re-signing the known-failing run ocidex-ocidex-push-lzrqc (cleared chains.tekton.dev/signed and /retries):
  - chains.tekton.dev/signed=true, no retries annotation (was failed / retries=3)
  - 1 Rekor upload (logIndex 2386121520), was 9
  - 10 OCI attestation uploads, was 90
  - 0 controller errors
  - cosign verify-attestation --key k8s://tekton-chains/signing-secrets --type slsaprovenance1 ghcr.io/pfenerty/ocidex-api@sha256:1fdbd09f... -> 'The signatures were verified against the specified public key'

Follow-up worth considering: the .att tags accumulated duplicate attestation layers from months of retry storms (ocidex-api's attestation bundle is now ~2.6MB). Not harmful, but could be pruned.
close_reason: Closed

Add the extension to node schematics, load the module, and deploy a tonistiigi/binfmt DaemonSet to register qemu handlers. Requires rolling node upgrades (reboots).
notes: 2026-10-13 backlog review: PARTLY DONE. The siderolabs/binfmt-misc extension is in WORKER_SCHEMATIC and the binfmt_misc module loads on x86-01 (patches/x86-01-network.yaml). Left: the tonistiigi/binfmt DaemonSet was removed because it registers qemu only inside its own mount namespace. A registrar that enters the host init namespace is needed. Acceptance (from closed apko-cicd-69w): a privileged TaskRun of 'melange build tools/gosec/melange.yaml --arch amd64,arm64' succeeds, then apko-cicd publishes multi-arch gosec.

title: Repair homelab Beads DB read inconsistency (embedded Dolt)
description: The homelab embedded-Dolt Beads DB returns a different issue set on every read path: bd list --status=all shows 6 issues, bd export writes a stale 3-issue subset (homelab-9o7, homelab-bhu, homelab-zjy), and bd show resolves IDs from both sets. bd create/update writes succeed and are visible via show/list, but auto-export to .beads/issues.jsonl fails (recurring 'auto-export: git add failed: exit status 1'), so issues.jsonl is stale and bd-all.nu under-reports homelab. bd dolt commit reports nothing to commit; bd doctor and bd dolt killall are unsupported in embedded mode. Likely working-set/index divergence or a partially-applied import. Investigate (bd dolt branches/log, consider bd init --force re-import from a known-good JSONL, or switch to server mode) and restore a single consistent view so issues.jsonl matches the DB.
acceptance_criteria: bd list, bd show, and bd export agree on the full issue set; .beads/issues.jsonl regenerates cleanly with all current issues; bd-all.nu lists homelab issues correctly; no recurring auto-export git-add failure.
notes: Parent epic: plan-bpo. Surfaced during post-migration review cleanup; blocks accurate cross-repo tracking.
close_reason: Fixed: root causes were (1) rogue nested .beads/.beads Dolt DB, (2) repos.additional multi-repo config, (3) beads version skew (0.42.0 vs 1.0.3) with mismatched daemons. Resolved by pinning beads=1.0.3 in common flox env, re-locking all repos, and pristine reinit-from-jsonl on a clean .beads. list/ready/show/stats/export now all consistent.

title: Tekton CI capacity: all pipeline pods land on the single x86-01 worker

x86-01 has 16GB RAM at ~37% use, so there is headroom, but there is no second worker to absorb a burst and no resource quota bounding a single pipeline run.

title: Automate etcd defrag on the RPi4 control plane
description:
etcd defrag is currently a manual talosctl procedure documented only in notes. In homelab-8md the DB had drifted to 204-212MB with 46MB in use (22% utilisation) before a manual defrag brought it to 46MB at 100%.

On SD-card storage, a bloated DB directly costs read latency because it stops fitting in page cache. Fragmentation will recur, so this needs to run on a schedule rather than when someone notices.

Note defrag blocks the member it runs on - any automation must do one node at a time with a quorum check between, exactly as the manual procedure does.

value: Never force-delete (k9s kill / --grace-period=0) a CNPG instance pod, especially ocidex-pg on local-path. CNPG stops the primary with a smart shutdown (stopDelay 1800s) that waits for app sessions. A force delete lets the replacement pod start a second postmaster on the same hostPath PGDATA, because PID and IPC namespaces hide the lock. That corrupted ocidex-pg's WAL on 2026-10-14 (homelab-8tp; recovered with pg_resetwal). Also, the Cluster's status.phase still reads 'healthy' right after a spec change, before the rollout starts, so wait on the pod instead.

synology-csi (updated 2026-10-13): default SC synology-csi-iscsi; node plugin + iscsi-tools only on x86-01, so every iSCSI consumer must pin kubernetes.io/arch: amd64 (trek, ocidex vuln-worker via HelmRelease postRenderers, ocidex-pg via Cluster spec.affinity.nodeSelector). The old 'first mkfs on >=10Gi exceeds the 2m NodeStage timeout' quirk was mkfs.ext4's whole-LUN discard (NAS UNMAPs at ~4 MB/s). A 60Gi format ran for 2h+, starved other LUNs' iSCSI sessions, and on 2026-10-13 took ocidex-pg's ext4 read-only (homelab-qlv). FIXED in f416036: SC parameter formatOptions: '-E nodiscard'; a 60Gi canary mounted in ~2 min. formatOptions only affects PVs provisioned after the change; SC parameters are immutable, so changes need kubectl delete sc + flux reconcile hr synology-csi --force. iSCSI replacement_timeout is 120s (iscsi-tools default). Server-side-apply error 'rollingUpdate: Forbidden when type is Recreate' on trek/ocidex vuln-worker was fixed by deleting the Deployment and reconciling.

Talos 1.14.0 gotcha (2026-10-10): a no-reboot apply-config that restarts the cri service leaves containerd stuck 'Waiting for service sandboxd to be registered' on every node (sandboxd is only registered at boot) -> all nodes NotReady. Fix: rolling reboot one node at a time (talosctl --talosconfig talos-cluster/talos/clusterconfig/talosconfig -e IP -n IP reboot). After make repatch-all, check 'talosctl services' for cri before walking away. Also: ~/.talos/config default context is ocidex-dev (127.0.0.1:63567) - always pass --talosconfig explicitly.

Talos multi-arch/binfmt VERIFIED state (2026-07): siderolabs/binfmt-misc extension + machine.kernel.modules[binfmt_misc] SUCCESSFULLY loads binfmt_misc.ko on the x86-01 worker (v1.13.4, kernel 6.18.34). Native amd64 melange builds work. BUT qemu cross-arch (arm64) still fails: the tonistiigi/binfmt DaemonSet (initContainer+pause) registers qemu in its OWN container mount-namespace binfmt_misc instance, which does NOT persist host-globally on Talos (Talos, unlike systemd distros, does not host-mount binfmt_misc). Kernel check via privileged pod confirmed qemu-aarch64 ABSENT after init exits. qemu-user-binfmt apk doesn't auto-register in a container; manual /proc/sys/fs/binfmt_misc/register write didn't take. FIX NEEDED: register in host init mount namespace (nsenter -t 1 -m + qemu-user-static). binfmt.kustomization.yaml left DISABLED. apko-cicd gosec builds run amd64-only until this is solved.
